claim: The strain of balancing a bicycle wrecks the nerves and leaves riders with a worn, grey 'bicycle face' (and even insanity).
what_happened: The 'bicycle face' vanished from medicine within a decade; cycling became a standard prescription for health.
lesson: When experts name a new disease after a new product, wait for the second study before you price it in.

quotes.text: what they call the "bicycle face" among their patrons One of them describes it as an anxious worn look the skin palid with a gray cast of complexion
quotes.speaker: English doctors (reported)

quotes.text: The "bicycle face" is a joke, and the "bicycle hump" is a prediction.
quotes.speaker: The San Francisco Examiner

quotes.text: The "monkey hump," the "bicycle face," "bicycle Insanity,"
quotes.speaker: Eddie C. Bald

claim: Hunching over the handlebars will give a generation a permanent 'bicycle stoop' or 'monkey hump' that ruins the nation's health.
what_happened: Riding posture changed with handlebar design; no national spinal epidemic appeared, and The Lancet itself blamed misuse, not the machine.
lesson: A real but fixable ergonomic flaw is a design brief, not a reason the product will fail.

quotes.text: I have been hesitating because I know if he rides very much he will become afflicted with the 'safety stoop.
quotes.speaker: a New York physician

quotes.text: One evil traceable to bicycling is the confirmed "stoop"
quotes.speaker: The Lancet (reported)
quotes.publication: Wilkes-Barre Times Leader, The Evening News

quotes.text: The monkey hump is injurious to the health of bicycle riders
quotes.speaker: E. Marguerite Lindley

claim: Heavy cycling damages the heart and kidneys and shortens life, so riders are bad insurance risks and unfit recruits.
what_happened: 'Bicycle heart' turned out to be the benign athlete's heart; cycling is now linked to lower cardiovascular mortality.
lesson: Gatekeepers who price risk (insurers, army doctors) can lock in a bad early theory, so put outcome data in front of them early.

quotes.text: Insurance Companies Awake to the Dangers of Bicycle Riding
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: too much bicycle riding was as bad for the kidneys
quotes.speaker: life insurance examiner (reported)

quotes.text: REJECTED FOR BICYCLE HEART
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: The bicycle caused the rise in appendicitis.
what_happened: Appendicitis was simply being diagnosed more; the Medical Record mocked the theory at the time.
lesson: A new thing's arrival lines up with every other trend of its decade; correlation in time is the cheapest accusation there is.

quotes.text: Bicycle Blamed for Appendicitis
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: Washington Physician Claims Disease Is Result fo Riding.
quotes.speaker: card subhead

claim: Children should perhaps not be allowed to ride at all, because they overdo it and injure themselves.
what_happened: Children's bikes became a near-universal part of childhood.
lesson: Fears aimed at children travel furthest; answer them with supervision rules, not prohibition.

quotes.text: it is an open question whether children should be permitted to ride at all
quotes.speaker: a physician 'of standing at the east'

claim: Cycling (and bloomers) will take women away from motherhood and the nursery.
what_happened: Women's cycling spread fast and became a symbol of the 'New Woman'; birth rates and family life were not undone by it.
lesson: When a tool expands one group's freedom, expect the objection to be framed as a health warning.

quotes.text: no hesitation in ndemning for women all those amusements or occupations which tend to take them from the nursery
quotes.speaker: Dr. Forbes Winslow

quotes.text: he prognosticates dire calamities to follow the New Woman's predilection for
quotes.speaker: Lucifer, the Light-Bearer

claim: Women on bicycles, especially in bloomers, are enemies of the Bible; the bicycle and infidelity go together.
what_happened: Within a few years clergy were riding too; the bloomer became ordinary sportswear.
lesson: Moral objections built on scripture age fastest, because the next generation of the same clergy adopts the thing.

quotes.text: A Georgia minister has been making quite a stir of late by classing women bicyclists among the enemies of the Bible. The bicycle and infidelity, he exclaims, go together.
quotes.speaker: Rutland Daily Herald

quotes.text: MORALS OF WHEELWOMEN
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: The bicycle frees young women from chaperones, making them loud, unladylike and even smokers.
what_happened: The freedom part was true, and later celebrated as women's emancipation; the predicted moral collapse did not follow.
lesson: A fear that is really a complaint about the thing working (people got freedom) is a sign the product has found its users.

quotes.text: with the wheel parties has arisen a freedom of manner unknown in the presence of the chaperon
quotes.speaker: The Daily Telegraph (reported)

quotes.text: No result of the bicycle craze is more conspicuous than that the woman who speaks In quiet modulated tones has departed perhaps forever
quotes.speaker: The Chicago Chronicle

quotes.text: THE BICYCLE GIRL Is a Symbol of the Progress and Glory Which Have Made the Century Glorious.
quotes.speaker: Ellis Parker Butler

claim: Sunday cycling is emptying the churches and weaning souls from heaven.
what_happened: US church membership kept rising into the 1950s; the bicycle boom faded within a few years.
lesson: Institutions that compete for the same hours (church, theatre, TV) are the first to call a new pastime a moral danger.

quotes.text: It has to stand considerable criticism as being, if not agency of his satanic majesty for the weaning away of souls from heaven.
quotes.speaker: The Times

claim: Young men love their bicycles more than their sweethearts, so marriages are falling off and couples are splitting.
what_happened: Marriage rates were driven by the economy, not the wheel; the tandem became a courting vehicle.
lesson: 'It's replacing human relationships' is said of every absorbing new hobby; measure the relationships, not the hobby.

quotes.text: It is claimed the young men go off on their wheels and leave the young ladies to themselves.
quotes.speaker: The Kenney Gazette

quotes.text: "they love their bicycles better than their sweethearts,"
quotes.speaker: a correspondent

claim: Cycling is killing the book trade, because riders are too busy or too tired to read.
what_happened: Book sales recovered as the craze cooled; reading survived the bicycle, radio, TV and the internet in turn.
lesson: Incumbents read a dip in their own numbers as proof of a newcomer's damage; check whether the dip outlasts the craze.

quotes.text: The latest charge brought against the bicycle is that it injures the booksellers trade.
quotes.speaker: Western Newspaper Union

quotes.text: Do Bicycle's Hurt Books?
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Cheap bicycle suits worn all day are destroying the custom tailoring trade.
what_happened: Custom tailoring did decline over the next century, but because of ready-to-wear manufacturing, not bicycle suits.
lesson: A trade in long decline will blame whatever is new that season; find the real driver before you cast the villain.

quotes.text: it has spoiled the regular tailoring trade
quotes.speaker: a striking tailors' leader

quotes.text: The bicycle is blamed for pretty much everything but the rainy weather.
quotes.speaker: card note

claim: Cycling is draining customers from theatres, dance halls, music teachers, seedsmen and art dealers.
what_happened: These trades recovered as the 1890s boom cooled; at the time even the Washington Post said the theatres had themselves to blame.
lesson: When a new pastime takes your customers' hours, the bigger risk is the excuse it gives you not to fix your product.

quotes.text: Certain music teachers of London protest that the bicycle is ruining their profession.
quotes.speaker: The Boston Globe

quotes.text: Bicycling has killed gardening for women.
quotes.speaker: The Buffalo Enquirer

quotes.text: Managers are losing money, because they no longer please the nubile taste.
quotes.speaker: The Washington Post (reprinted)

claim: The bicycle is behind low crop prices, slow shops, empty bars and even poor fishing.
what_happened: The real cause was the depression after the Panic of 1893; once the economy recovered, the bicycle stopped being blamed.
lesson: In a downturn the most visible new thing becomes the scapegoat, and the blame says more about the downturn than the product.

quotes.text: The farmer complains of low prices :of corn. Cause, bicycles
quotes.speaker: Staunton Spectator and Vindicator

quotes.text: by common consent, the bicycle has been blamed during the last few years- for every change in business conditions.
quotes.speaker: The Buffalo Times

quotes.text: I don't know everybody says it's the bicycle, you see.
quotes.speaker: a New York fisherman

claim: The bicycle boom is a bubble that will collapse.
what_happened: The boom did collapse: by 1897 there was overproduction and $100 bikes sold for $40. But the bicycle stayed, and by 1904 dealers reported rising sales again.
lesson: A bubble in the industry and a fad in the product are different bets: the companies can crash while the thing becomes permanent.

quotes.text: when do you think thia bicycle bubble will collapse
quotes.speaker: a carriage and wagon wheel manufacturer

quotes.text: Official Report Says England Had an Over-Production of Bicycles Last Year.
quotes.speaker: US Consul Barker (reported)

quotes.text: Whoever has been telling about the premature death and practical extermination of the bicycle, has been revising his decision
quotes.speaker: The Fall River Daily Herald

claim: The bicycle will put the pleasure horse out of use (horse breeders' fear, which they dismissed in print).
what_happened: Horse prices rose while bicycle prices fell; the bicycle never replaced the horse, but the car did within about 20 years.
lesson: Seeing off the first challenger is not safety; the incumbent who wins against a weak substitute often stops watching for the strong one.

quotes.text: A couple of years ago a great many people exclaimed that the horse would go out of use as a source ot pleasure, and that the bicycle would take hit place
quotes.speaker: American Horse Breeder (reprinted)

claim: Bicycles frighten horses and cause runaways, so they should be banned from parks and roads.
what_happened: Riders showed that very few horses shied; park bans were contested in court and lifted; horses later left the roads altogether.
lesson: A ban justified by the incumbent's fragility (skittish horses) dies with the incumbent.

quotes.text: the practice is nevertheless fraught with great danger to the public, especially those who drive or ride spirited horses
quotes.speaker: The Bury and Norwich Post

quotes.text: tho horse was frightened by a passing bicycle," is always prominent
quotes.speaker: a Brooklyn reader

claim: Bicycles are a nuisance and a danger to people on foot and should be driven off the streets and sidewalks.
what_happened: The conflict was real and got settled by rules (lamps after dark, no riding on footways), not by banning bikes.
lesson: When a complaint is real, offer the rule that answers it before someone else writes the ban.

quotes.text: Did it ever occur to you what infernal nuisances those confounded bicycles are?
quotes.speaker: a 'communicative man'

quotes.text: A Bicyclist shall not ride or impel his Bicycle upon any footway, pavement, or causeway made or set apart for the use or accemmodation of foot passengers.
quotes.speaker: bye-laws

claim: The velocipede is pointless; it is no different from walking.
what_happened: Once the safety bicycle arrived in the late 1880s it became the most efficient human-powered transport ever made.
lesson: Early versions get judged as they are, not as they'll become; 'no better than walking' was true of the velocipede and false of the bicycle.

quotes.text: People didn’t see the point or why it was any different from walking
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Cycling makes people selfish.
what_happened: No lasting character effect was ever shown; group rides and clubs became a big part of social life.
lesson: Claims about character are easy to make and impossible to test, so they fade without being refuted.

quotes.text: Does Bicycling Increase Selfishness?
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Even with the speed limit lifted there is 'no scope for carriages without horses'; the car is an amusing toy for adults.
what_happened: The Red Flag Act was repealed later in 1896; Merryweather & Sons, the horse-drawn fire-engine builder, went on to sell motor fire engines.
lesson: The incumbent who calls the new thing a toy is often the one who ends up selling it, so dismiss it in private and prototype it in public.

quotes.text: there could be no scope for carriages without horses
quotes.speaker: Mr. Merryweather
quotes.publication: The Yorkshire Herald and the York Herald

quotes.text: an amusing toy for adults
quotes.speaker: Mr. Merryweather
quotes.publication: The Yorkshire Herald and the York Herald

quotes.text: If he lives to be many years older, he will find out his mistake.
quotes.speaker: The Yorkshire Herald
quotes.publication: The Yorkshire Herald and the York Herald

claim: Cars won't replace the horse; the horseless age is a dream far in the future, and the numbers prove the horse is holding its own.
what_happened: US horse numbers did keep rising until about 1915, then fell by roughly 90% over the next 40 years as cars, trucks and tractors took over.
lesson: The incumbent's numbers can still be going up when the disruption has already started, so watch the challenger's growth rate, not the incumbent's total.

quotes.text: It is an iridescent dream, hardly up to a disturbing nightmare.
quotes.speaker: American Sportsman (reprinted)

quotes.text: I do not think they will ever take the place of our noble horses especially on the farm.
quotes.speaker: Capt. George Shebron

quotes.text: Statistics Show Passing of Horse a Motor Myth
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: The automobile is useless in war and won't replace the cavalry horse.
what_happened: Motor trucks were decisive logistics in WWI, and by WWII armies were mechanized.
lesson: Professionals whose status rests on the old tool are the slowest to see the new one, and the military shows this most clearly.

quotes.text: Automobile Useless in War "Won't Supplant Horse"
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: I think it will be a great many years before autos taka the plane of horses In the army.
quotes.speaker: Capt. George Shebron

claim: Horseless carriages frighten horses and cause runaways, so they should be banned from city streets and parks.
what_happened: The bans fell within a few years (the Philadelphia park commission was already being pushed to give way in 1899); the horses were the ones that left.
lesson: Rules written to protect the old system's weak spot have a clock on them; build for the world after they lapse.

quotes.text: the commissioners placed a ban on all horseless vehicles on the ground that they frighten horse and are likely to cause runaways and accidents.
quotes.speaker: The Weekly Leader

quotes.text: "Devil wagon" was the 1902 motor car.
quotes.speaker: Kansas City Star (reprinted)

claim: Fast automobiles are a terror on the roads; speeds should be capped near horse pace and fast cars should not even be built.
what_happened: The danger was real: road deaths reached tens of thousands a year in the US. Speed caps near horse pace failed; licensing, road design and safety engineering cut the death rate per mile instead.
lesson: When the harm is real, the winning answer is engineering and rules that let the thing scale, not limits that make it pointless.

quotes.text: Automobile Terror
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: People wanted to prohibit construction of automobiles that could go more than 20MPH
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: Law is proposed to jail automobile drivers going more than 5MPH above average speed of horse and buggy
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Cars will never be affordable to ordinary people the way bicycles are, and a horse is cheaper to keep.
what_happened: The Model T came out in 1908 and its price fell below $300 by the mid-1920s; car ownership became a mass-market thing.
lesson: Never judge a manufactured product's future market by its first price; cost curves are what make mass markets.

quotes.text: Will never be affordable like bicycle
quotes.speaker: card note

quotes.text: Dobbin is worth what you paid for him two years ago, where's the man with an auto that can say the same?
quotes.speaker: a harness dealer's advertisement

claim: Driving gives people an 'automobile face', an 'automobile eye' and an 'automobile brain' from the nervous strain.
what_happened: Like the bicycle face, these syndromes vanished from medicine.
lesson: When a 'face' or 'brain' diagnosis has been pinned on each new device in turn, treat the next one as a template, not a finding.

quotes.text: The automobile face is no joke.
quotes.speaker: Henri Fournier

quotes.text: The Automobile Brain
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: A NEW AUTOMOBILE AND AEROPLANE DISEASE
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Riding instead of walking is making people lazy, and laziness is a growing sin.
what_happened: Car dependence really is tied to less physical activity and to obesity, but the moral framing was wrong and the car's benefits won.
lesson: Some fears about effort-saving tools turn out right about the side effect and wrong about the verdict, so design for the side effect.

quotes.text: Laziness Growing Sin, Learned Doctor Says
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Night-time car rides (along with jazz and cards) are breaking up the home and causing divorce.
what_happened: The car did move courtship out of the parlour, but the family survived it; divorce trends had much bigger causes.
lesson: A product that changes where people meet will be blamed for whatever happens next in those relationships.

quotes.text: Pastor Denounces Autos
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: AUTOMOBILE BLAMED FOR A DIVORCE SUIT
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: With jazz music, jazz amusements, jazz reading, jazz conversation, jazz ornaments
quotes.speaker: Southern Presbyterian Committee on Sabbath and Family Religion

claim: Radios in cars will distract drivers and should be banned.
what_happened: Car radios became standard equipment with no measurable crash epidemic; distraction worries came back with phones, which really are a risk.
lesson: Each new screen or speaker in the car gets the same safety fear; what matters is how much it pulls the driver's eyes and hands.

quotes.text: Automobile Radio Ban Proposals
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Motor cabs will take the livelihood of horse cabmen and their families.
what_happened: The horse cab disappeared from London within about 20 years, but many cabmen kept driving and moved to motor taxis. The job survived and the horse didn't.
lesson: Automation more often changes the job than ends it; give the incumbents a path onto the new machine and the fight shrinks.

quotes.text: Another modern improvement has called forth a protest from those who must Inevitably suffer from It introduction.
quotes.speaker: The Nebraska State Journal

quotes.text: London Cabbies Last Days
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: The car will wipe out the livery stables and the horse trades.
what_happened: It did. By 1918 livery stables were called 'relics', and by 1930 city horse jobs needed defending; Miami Beach became horseless in 1968.
lesson: When the incumbent's fear is the business model itself being replaced, it is usually right; the question is whether you move or not.

quotes.text: Livery Stables Are Relics of the Past Now
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: Old Dobbin's Friends Rally To Save His Job With City
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: Miami Becomes Horseless City
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: A true flying machine is impossible; the obstacles can never be overcome.
what_happened: The Wright brothers flew in 1903, twelve years after Hazen's statement.
lesson: 'Impossible' from an eminent scientist usually means nobody has found the method yet; ask what specific obstacle they mean and watch for it to fall.

quotes.text: A pure flying-machine is impossible, asserts Professor Joseph LeConte.
quotes.speaker: Prof. Joseph LeConte

quotes.text: He Says there are insurmountable obstacles to perfecting a flying-machine, which Prof. Langley and other scientists will never be able to overcome.
quotes.speaker: Prof. Hazen, US Signal Office

claim: The motor scooter will add new terrors to city life.
what_happened: The Autoped faded commercially by the early 1920s before it could terrorise anyone; the idea came back a century later as the e-scooter.
lesson: A product can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the fear about it, and the idea can still come back later.

quotes.text: Might Add New-Terrors to City Life
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: The new telephone line caused the drop in cotton prices.
what_happened: Cotton prices followed world markets; the phone just made price news travel faster, which helped farmers more than it hurt them.
lesson: People who don't understand how a technology works will blame it for whatever goes wrong when it arrives; showing them how it works is the fix.

quotes.text: being unable to account for the slump in any other way, laid it to the telephone.
quotes.speaker: The Yazoo Herald

claim: Wiring the globe with telegraph lines could disturb the earth's currents and throw nature into disorder.
what_happened: Telegraph and then telephone networks covered the planet with no such effect.
lesson: Fears that scale up a technology to planetary disaster are cheap to raise; ask for the mechanism and a magnitude.

quotes.text: Global telegraphy could screw with earths currents and disorder the universe.
quotes.speaker: card note

quotes.text: A Telegraphic Cataclysm
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Edison has invented too many harmful things and his new devices will cause social chaos (written as satire).
what_happened: Edison's phonograph, electric light and power systems became the backbone of modern life.
lesson: Even mocking pieces about too much invention show what people are anxious about; the anxiety is real even when the threat is a joke.

quotes.text: Mr. Edison has invent ed too many things
quotes.speaker: The New York Times (reprinted)

claim: There are so many stations that the airwaves are jammed; there is 'too much music in the air.'
what_happened: The interference was real and got worse until the Radio Act of 1927 set up licensing; then radio grew into a mass medium.
lesson: A shared resource that new entrants crowd (spectrum, airspace, roads) needs rules; supporting the rules early is how you keep the market open.

quotes.text: TOO MUCH MUSIC IN THE AIR NOW
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Movies, radio and cheap newspapers (and mass education) are the troublemakers that caused the war.
what_happened: Nazi propaganda really did use radio and film well, but mass media and education went on to underpin postwar democracies.
lesson: A medium can amplify the worst actors and still be good overall; the business question is who controls distribution.

quotes.text: the movies, the radio and cheap newspapers . . . are the great trouble makers.
quotes.speaker: H. B. Parker, former Westmount High principal

claim: Children are watching too much TV and falling asleep in class ('tele-snoozing').
what_happened: Later research did link heavy childhood screen time to less sleep and attention problems, though TV didn't ruin a generation.
lesson: The sleep-and-attention fear has come back for every screen and is partly right each time, so build in limits instead of denying it.

quotes.text: Too much television and not eonugh sleep is becoming a school room problem
quotes.speaker: A. Whipple, Rhode Island College of Education (reported in an ad)

claim: The gadget-packed 'labour-saving house' is a Frankenstein monster that only trades physical work for mental work.
what_happened: Appliances cut drudgery a lot, but historians found housework hours fell much less than promised as standards rose ('more work for mother').
lesson: Saving labour often raises the standard instead of freeing time, so sell what people get, not the hours they'll save.

quotes.text: a veritable Frankenstein monster, which inventors have jokingly nicknamed the "labor saving house.
quotes.speaker: David G. Bareuther, AP

claim: Machines like the steam shovel are taking jobs from unemployed men.
what_happened: Mechanical excavation did replace hand-digging gangs, but overall employment recovered and construction grew.
lesson: Job fears peak in recessions, when machines and hard times arrive together; the anger targets the machine either way.

quotes.text: Use of the steam shovel was protested some time ago by Quebec unemployed, who claimed it was displacing men from work.
quotes.speaker: Canadian Press

claim: Postcards and the typewriter are killing the art of letter-writing.
what_happened: Long personal letters did decline over the century, but total written communication exploded through postcards, phones, then email and text.
lesson: A lighter format replaces a heavier one and people call it a loss of craft; usually both the loss and the gain are real.

quotes.text: I doubt very much If there Is one family in a hundred nowadays whose members Indulge in the good old fashion of writing sensible, readable letters
quotes.speaker: a correspondent to the New York Sun

claim: Writing on a typewriter harms literature.
what_happened: Most writers ended up drafting on typewriters, then word processors.
lesson: Craftspeople argue about a new tool and then quietly adopt it, which is the likely path for AI writing tools too.

quotes.text: Ten Authors Speak For and Against It as an Aid to Literature
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Automatic lifts without an operator are unsafe and should be banned.
what_happened: Operatorless lifts became universal and very safe; the operator job disappeared instead.
lesson: Taking the human operator out feels unsafe long after it actually is; trust comes from familiarity, not statistics.

quotes.text: Automatic Lift Ban
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Cheap candies (including liquor-filled 'brandy drops' and gum lotteries) are harming children's health and morals.
what_happened: Adulterated candies with toxic dyes were a real problem fixed by pure-food laws like the 1906 US act; candy itself stayed.
lesson: A real quality problem in a new category gets solved by standards, and the category grows afterwards; be the brand that pushes for the standards.

quotes.text: CHEAP CANDIES AND THE HEALTH OF BROOKLYN.
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: NO MORE "BRANDY DROPS" FOR CHILDREN. As Much Alcohol in Six of the Candies as in a Cocktail.
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Too much theatre debases young men and drives boys to violence.
what_happened: Theatre and then cinema became mass entertainment with no wave of youth violence attributable to them.
lesson: Stories about one violent kid and one new medium sell newspapers and rarely survive population data.

quotes.text: Perhaps the earliest results of the debasing influences of the theatres
quotes.speaker: card quote

quotes.text: 15-year-old whipped his mother and drew revolver on her and his sister - too much theatre blamed.
quotes.speaker: card note

claim: Frequent theatre-going, among other bad habits, raises the chance of getting tuberculosis and shortens American lives.
what_happened: TB deaths fell steeply between 1920 and 1950 while movie-going boomed.
lesson: If the feared harm falls while use of the thing explodes, the fear was wrong.

quotes.text: Blaming too much theatre-going among other things for increasing chances of getting Tuberculosis
quotes.speaker: card note

quotes.text: Theatre going blamed for low-average age in the United States.
quotes.speaker: card note

claim: Jazz is making girls delinquent and has put American morals 'in a state of jazz'.
what_happened: Jazz became a national art form taught in conservatories; even officials of the day couldn't tie specific delinquency cases to it.
lesson: When even the officials can't name one case, the fear is about the culture, not the product.

quotes.text: Jazz Blamed For Delinquency of Girls of Today
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: With jazz music, jazz amusements, jazz reading, jazz conversation, jazz ornaments
quotes.speaker: Southern Presbyterian Committee on Sabbath and Family Religion

quotes.text: Jazz Compared to smoking
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Jazz mania drives young people to murder.
what_happened: Newspapers of the time pointed out that the stories gave no causal link; jazz has no place in any later crime research.
lesson: A headline blaming a new thing for a crime is often contradicted by its own story, so read to the end.

quotes.text: JAZZ BLAMED FOR MURDER
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: Yet jazz is blamed offhand, as though there were no doubt about it at all.
quotes.speaker: The Daily Sentinel

quotes.text: Jazz Is Blamed In Double Murder
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Jazz and the jazz-age pace cause goiter, indigestion and body ailments unknown to the ancients.
what_happened: No such link was ever found; restaurant music became normal.
lesson: When the same new thing is blamed for many unrelated illnesses, it is a stand-in for discomfort with change.

quotes.text: NOW JAZZ IS BLAMED FOR BODY AILMENTS
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: JAZZ MUSIC BLAMED NOW, FOR INDIGESTION.
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Modern 'jazz' books are turning teenagers into conceited prigs and causing a wave of youth suicides.
what_happened: No link between popular literature and youth suicide was established; the panic moved on to comics, then TV.
lesson: Youth-suicide panics attach to whatever teenagers are reading or watching, and they deserve evidence, not reflex.

quotes.text: JAZZ BOOKS BLAMED FOR YOUTHS' SUICIDES
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: brood of the most conceited and insufferable little prigs that ever happened.
quotes.speaker: State Senator William L. Love

claim: A hit song inspires listeners to suicide and should be banned.
what_happened: The 'Hungarian suicide song' story became an urban legend; no causal link was shown.
lesson: Content panics grow on a few tragic anecdotes; answer with data and care, not denial.

quotes.text: The song that Hungary outlawed because it Inspired thoughts of suicide
quotes.speaker: AP

quotes.text: Song Blamed For Suicide of Youth
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Pedestrians wearing headphones in both ears are a danger and should be banned from doing so.
what_happened: The ban was dropped; distracted-walking injuries are real but rare, and attention moved to phones.
lesson: When a risk is real but small, laws struggle to pass and design or education fixes tend to win.

quotes.text: an Arkansas state senator on Tuesday dropped his proposal to ban pedestrians from wearing headphones in both ears while on the street or sidewalk.
quotes.speaker: AP

claim: The new dances are corrupting the youth of the country.
what_happened: Each 'scandalous' dance became the next generation's respectable ballroom standard.
lesson: Today's scandalous youth culture is tomorrow's nostalgia; don't build your positioning around condemning it.

quotes.text: DANCES CORRUPTING YOUTH OF THE LAND
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: The dance problem is now a boy's problem as well as a girl's problem.
quotes.speaker: G. E. Johnson, New York School of Philanthropy

quotes.text: Demoralising Dances. NEWFANGLED frivolities. CORRUPTION AND SCANDAL OF WORST TYPE.
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: The waltz is demoralising and improper, scandalous enough to end in a duel.
what_happened: The waltz became the most respectable dance in the ballroom within a generation.
lesson: Something shocking because it is intimate tends to become normal fast once the next generation grows up with it.

quotes.text: THE DUEL (Globe - Friday 24 July 1812)
quotes.speaker: card headline

quotes.text: Concerns about demoralizing dance at inaugural presidential ball.
quotes.speaker: card headline

claim: Scanty bathing suits are indecent and must be policed off the beaches.
what_happened: Enforcement fell apart; by the 1940s topless men and one-piece suits were normal.
lesson: Decency rules that fine people a dollar are a sign the norm has already moved.

quotes.text: Refusing to attempt to cloak too scantily clad beach bathers by law and rule and ordinance
quotes.speaker: Los Angeles county beach authorities

quotes.text: Ocean City Turns Thumbs Down On Bare-chested Beach Tarzans
quotes.speaker: headline

quotes.text: because they don't spend any money
quotes.speaker: Police Chief Robert J. Lackey

claim: Voting will corrupt women.
what_happened: Colorado's experience showed polls became more orderly; suffrage went national in 1920.
lesson: Early adopter regions are the best test of a fear; point to them.

quotes.text: Instead of woman's going to the polls corrupting women, it has purified the polls.
quotes.speaker: Hon. John F. Shafroth

claim: If the Republicans win they will divide property, destroy the constitution and burn the churches.
what_happened: Five or six years of Republican rule did none of this, as their own supporters pointed out in 1805.
lesson: Incumbents losing power predict catastrophe, and a few years of real results is the best answer.

quotes.text: To destroy the constitution
quotes.speaker: Federalist charge (recalled)

quotes.text: To burn the churches
quotes.speaker: Federalist charge (recalled)

claim: This is the most important election ever.
what_happened: The same line ran in 1813, 1824, 1864, 1923 and 1936, and the republic outlived every one.
lesson: If urgency is claimed every cycle it means nothing; save your 'this changes everything' for when it's true.

quotes.text: the most important election in the history of this nation
quotes.speaker: Vermont Chronicle

quotes.text: This is the most important election In our lifetime.
quotes.speaker: Secretary of State Atwood

claim: America has no more room for immigrants.
what_happened: The population more than doubled over the next 60 years, and the economy grew with it.
lesson: 'The market is full' is usually a feeling, not a measurement, so check the numbers.

quotes.text: ridiculing the notion far too popular nowadays that we have no more room for immigrants
quotes.speaker: Edward Atkinson (reported)

claim: Hordes of immigrants are driving a crime wave.
what_happened: The Dillingham Commission (1911) found no evidence that immigration raised crime; later research finds immigrants offend at lower rates.
lesson: A visible newcomer gets blamed for a crime wave before anyone counts.

quotes.text: Hordes of immigrants, Including thousands ot criminals and the "scum of Europe,"
quotes.speaker: NYC Police Commissioner Bingham (reported)

claim: Immigrants are causing unemployment for native workers.
what_happened: Economists find small, concentrated wage effects on close substitutes and little overall unemployment effect; unions pushed through the 1920s quotas anyway.
lesson: Labour-substitution fears are partly right for the closest substitutes and wrong overall, so be specific about who actually loses.

quotes.text: The influx of immigrants in to the United States is blamed by the Illinois Federation of labor for the shortage of employment
quotes.speaker: Illinois Federation of Labor

claim: The alien population is driving up insanity, which will double or treble within 50 years.
what_happened: The prediction rested on diagnostic and institutional trends, not on immigrants; it fed eugenic immigration restriction instead.
lesson: Trend lines projected 50 years ahead are where bad fears hide; check what is being measured.

quotes.text: RUM AND IMMIGRATION BLAMED FOR INSANITY
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Unvaccinated immigrants threaten a new smallpox epidemic.
what_happened: Imported smallpox cases were a real risk before eradication, and the fix the doctor asked for, vaccinating everyone, worked; no major epidemic followed.
lesson: When the fear points to a fix that works, push for the fix rather than the restriction.

quotes.text: IMMIGRANTS ARE BLAMED Threat of Smallpox Epidemic Spreading in France
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: Flu masks are harmful because they block fresh air, and they don't keep out germs anyway.
what_happened: 1918 gauze masks did seem to have little effect on city-level case curves, but the 'harmful' claim was wrong; mask fights came back almost word for word in 2020.
lesson: A public-health measure can be weak in effect and still harmless; keep the two claims separate.

quotes.text: the masks "are harmful to the wearers, in that they prevent the free breathing of fresh air, essential at this time, and that they do not keep out the germs,"
quotes.speaker: Dr. G. M. Corput, US Public Health Service

quotes.text: shows little .if any influence from the compulsory wearing ofmasks
quotes.speaker: W. H. Kellogg, California State Board of Health

quotes.text: it has been decided by prominent doctors that the gauze mask was more of a menace than a benefit.
quotes.speaker: The Idaho Republican

claim: Women's revealing new fashions are spreading influenza.
what_happened: Flu spreads through the air between people, not through bare legs; hemlines kept rising.
lesson: A health scare can be a moral complaint dressed up in medical language; ask whether the mechanism holds up.

quotes.text: FEMININE DRESS BLAMED FOR FLU
quotes.speaker: headline

claim: The craze for growing pears is a speculative mania like the tulip mania.
what_happened: Pear growing became an ordinary orchard industry rather than a crash; the writer rejected the tulip comparison at the time.
lesson: Not every boom is a tulip mania; ask whether demand is real and repeats (food) or purely speculative.

quotes.text: The Pear Mania.
quotes.speaker: B. Hodge

claim: The fashionable metal brush and hundred-stroke routine damage the scalp.
what_happened: The warning was mostly right: over-brushing with hard bristles irritates the scalp, and the fad faded.
lesson: Sometimes the sceptic of a wellness fad is right; a product that hurts its users fades without anyone banning it.

quotes.text: very few scalps can stand the painful effects o the metal teeth in these brushes
quotes.speaker: The Philadelphia Inquirer

claim: Dismissal: modern war is becoming less destructive relative to population (the fear of mechanized slaughter is overblown).
what_happened: WWII killed about 70-85 million people, around 3% of the world's population, far more than the chart's WWI benchmark.
lesson: Reassuring trend charts about a new destructive power can break exactly when the new power gets used at scale.

quotes.text: modern wars are becoming less destructive
quotes.speaker: The Tribune
